A platoon of militia dressed in the same uniform as Matkina and yourself approaches. In the back, a conspicuous figure in a decorative mask watches impassively.

A man in front, decorated more lavishly than his fellow soldiers, approaches.
From Tash's memories that you've already seen, you recognize him as Colonel Ledak, your superior officer.
A horn of polished synth hangs from his belt.
It looks like it would fit the empty hole you found in the cave almost exactly.
"Matkina. Tash." He nods at each of you in turn. "What do you have to report?"
"Nothing, sir. We found where we believe the jahk used to be, but it's gone, and the villagers don't have it."
"Nothing, sir. We didn't find the jahk. I don't believe it's in the village at all."
"I see. Do you have anything else to report?" He looks at you expectantly.
"Yes, sir. Matkina came to warn the villagers of the attack."
"Yes, sir. You were right about Matkina: she warned the villagers of the attack."
"No, sir."
(Lie) "No, sir."
"Is that the jahk at your side, sir?"
"What?" She turns to you, eyes wet. Suddenly her countenance transforms into hot rage. "You lying bastard!"
Matkina turns on you with a death glare. Before she can do anything, Ledak snaps his fingers and the other militia members grab Matkina and hold her in place.
She leaps to attack you, but Ledak's arm is a blur, slashing Matkina's face with jagged metal. She cries out as the other militia members surround her and hold her in place.

"Didn't I tell you her love for the villagers was stronger?" He turns to face the masked figure and gives a slight, royal bow.

"It's not often I am right and the First is wrong," he confides as he turns back to you. "Now, I believe you deserve the full truth"

"That's good to hear." He turns toward the masked figure and gives a deep, royal bow.

"Once again, the First proves her wisdom," he says when he turns back to you. "Since that is done, I believe you deserve the full truth."
"Do you know what the jahk does, sir?"
"What is that, sir?"
"What will happen to Matkina?"
He gives you a wry smile. "Unusually astute of you, Tash. You are right, of course."
"I apologize for wasting your time. We always knew the jahk was not in the village, or rather we knew that it was *once* in the village."
"You were never meant to find the jahk. This mission was a ruse to draw out Matkina's loyalty -- a wildly successful ruse, I might add."

He takes the horn off his belt and lifts it up. Moonlight glints off its golden surface. "The First came here years ago, posing as an Aeon Priest. She's had the jahk for some time. We're going to use it to capture the villagers."
"She will be dealt with as the traitor she is. You have completed your true mission."
"All in good time. You have earned the knowledge, of course, though I'm afraid the artifact was never your true mission."
"How will the jahk help us capture the villagers?"
"Why is the attack necessary?"
"What? Why? You have the jahk. The villagers have nothing!"
"The villagers are a danger, as you know well. They are also a potential boon to us. We *will* capture them."
"Not while I can stop you." Matkina's blade flashes in her hands and she attacks.
[Attack] Join her.
Forcibly stop her.
"Matkina, stop!"
Do nothing.
"Two traitors then."
You grab her arms before she's able to strike Colonel Ledak. She struggles, cutting you in the process.
You try to grab her, but she pulls out of your grip and lunges at Colonel Ledak.
She ignores you and lunges at Colonel Ledak.
Ledak's arm is a blur, slashing Matkina's face with jagged metal. She cries out as the other militia members grab her and remove her weapons.
"So I was right after all. Her love for the villagers *is* stronger. It was fortunate we discovered her treachery now, before the attack."
"May I see the jahk, sir?"
"Was that really necessary, sir?"
His eyes narrow. "You sound soft, Sergeant. Don't let it happen again or I will treat you as a traitor as well."

"It's a powerful artifact from a prior world, as you no doubt have guessed. It's possible it can be configured to do many things, but for us it will nullify the power of the teratomorphs, making them quail like cowed pups."
"I thought the village only cared for one teratomorph."
"I'm ready to fight, sir. Let's head to the village."
"To Kholn Village, brothers!"
"Is that what she told you? She lied to you as well, then, Tash. *Many* in the village are teratomorphs."
"What is a teratomorph?"
"What's a teratomorph again?"

"A kind of skin-dancer or lycanthrope. You no doubt saw one while you were in the village, though I doubt you'd recognize it in its human form.

"A teratomorph is like a person, but with an ability -- or a disease, depending on who you talk to -- that transforms them into a monstrous tentacled creature during the day."
"A skin-dancer and a horrible beast."
He looks at you suspiciously. "I *know* I've told you. The Sand Knights have traced the source of the teratomorph attacks to this village -- our own sources confirm it. They will be here soon."
Fear blooms on Matkina's face. "Why didn't you tell me before?"
"Because *you* would've insisted we defend them at any cost. The First..." He looks respectfully back at the masked figure. "...has different plans."

"We must get there first. The villagers will not come peacefully, we know that." He gives Matkina a meaningful look as he says this. "But if we can capture some of the teratomorphs, we can spare them a terrible death whilst bolstering our own strength against the Changing God."
"Liar! She serves her own ends. No one elses!"
Colonel Ledak looks to the sky in exasperation. "It's *called* the greater good."
"He's right, Matkina. They're doomed either way."
"She's right, Ledak. We should help them, not take what we can and run."
"That answers my question."
"Are we ready to go then?"
"But if the militia helped them, think how much more willingly they would serve the First. What she's doing is the easiest way, but not the best. Not by far."
"You've *met* them. Do they seem like murderers to you? The only murderer here stands in front of you." She glares at Ledak.
"He's talking about murder and slavery. If the First really wants to serve the greater good, she would find a way that benefits all, not just herself."
"There is *no* justification for slaughtering innocents. That's what they're doing."
She gives you a pleading look. "You have a chance to be a hero now. To me and my people, if no one else."
"Everyone dies, Sergeant, even us. With the Sand Knights involved, we cannot hope to stop the deaths of the villagers. We *can* save their culture and knowledge, though, by sparing a few."
"You have seen what the Sand Knights do to their victims, Tash. If we do nothing, we condemn them to a pointless and horrible death. Those we can save, however, have a chance to make a difference."
"We *cannot* help them. If we tried, we would only die with them, and our cause would die with us."
"We *are* helping them, in the only way we can."
"If we hope to gain any power -- over the Sand Knights or our titular sire -- we *must* see this through."
"I'm sorry, Matkina, but I think Ledak is right."
"You've lost this, Matkina. Ledak is right."
"He's right, Matkina."
"No, sir. I cannot condone this."
"She makes a good point, Ledak."
"I have to side with Matkina, sir."
"I have to side with Ledak and the First."
"Then two traitors will die with the monsters."
[Attack] "Nobody's dying today but you."
[Attack] "Joke's on you. I can't die here."
[Attack] "Don't worry, Matkina. We'll get out of this."
"Brothers! Attack!"
"Worry about yourself."
"I was a fool to trust you. Or anyone."
"I think I've earned that honor, don't you?"
"That honor goes to the leader of the attack."
"You want to lead the attack?"
"Hm. Never mind, then."
"I suppose you have, Sergeant." He hands you the jahk. "Lead us to victory."
Colonel Ledak thinks it over. "The First gave this attack to me, Sergeant, and I will respect her wishes."
"Thank you, sir. Let's go."
"May I ask some questions about the attack?"
Destroy the jahk.

You drop the horn on the ground and crush it. Unfortunately, the synth it is made of proves tougher than your foot.

Ledak is not amused.

You drop the horn on the ground and stamp it with your foot. It shatters into dozens of synth shards.

Ledak is not amused.

Ledak frowns alarmingly. "That is not the sort of question I would expect from the man *leading* the attack. For your sake..." He glances nervously back at the First. "...I will pretend I did not hear it."
Ledak's look is menacing. "After requesting the honor of leading it? For your sake, I hope you are joking."
"Of course I am. Got you!"
"I'm serious. I think there's reason to believe we will fail."
Ledak frowns, supremely unamused.
[Attack] "Actually, I'm betraying you. Got you!"
Colonel Ledak laughs. "And what brought this on?"
"The village is home to a monster called a teratomorph."
"Sir, I believe we should call off the attack."
"I have another reason to believe we should call off the attack."
[Attack] "Because I won't let you."
Ledak throws his head back in howling laughter. "You..." He wipes away a tear. "You have been lied to, or else sorely misinformed. *Many* of the villagers are teratomorphs."
"We have the jahk. We shouldn't risk the men."
"Never mind. I... wasn't thinking straight."
"They know we're coming. They'll be ready."
"Yes, sir. We are going to stop you."
Matkina looks at you, her emotions rushing quickly from surprise to respect. At some point, her blade appears in her hand.
"They won't be ready for this." He pats the horn on his belt.
"They're preparing an ambush."
Ledak fumes. "What? Why?"
"I told them to."
(Lie) "Matkina told them to."
(Lie) "I overheard them say so."
"You lying rat sack. It was *your* plan! I only agreed with it."
"You lying rat sack. It was *your* plan!"
Ledak turns on you. "Is this true?"
"Yes."
"No. She's just trying to take me down with her."
"Of course. Well, rest assured that even an ambush won't save them, not as long as we have the jahk."
"Of course. Forgive me for doubting you. Rest assured that even an ambush won't save them, not as long as we have the jahk."
"We can't kill them, sir. It's not right."

"I'm surprised to hear you say that, and not pleased.

"We are not the ones to decide right or wrong, Sergeant. There is too much that we don't know.

"As for the villagers, the choice will be theirs. Indeed, it has been, and we are gracious to give them another one."
"Where is everyone? You were just here, Tash. What is going on?"
"The villagers are preparing to ambush."
"It could be an ambush. Perhaps we should reconsider our attack."
"I don't know, sir."
"What?" He turns on you. "How do you know this?"
"Of course. Well, rest assured that even an ambush won't save them."
Ledak points his blade at you. "It seems that two traitors will die with the monsters then."
[Attack] "Villagers! Attack!"
[Attack] "We'll see about that."
Run.
"Kill the traitor!"
"Even if it is an ambush, Gerave, there is no reason to call off the attack."
"We have nothing to fear, so long as we carry the jahk." He pats the horn on his belt. "Come, brothers. Let's see what's left for us here."
"We have nothing to fear, so long as we have the jahk." He reaches for the horn by his belt and finds it missing. "What? Where is it?"
Attack him.
Follow him.
"Stay alert, brothers."
"I took it from you while your back was turned."
"I have it. Call off the attack, Ledak."
"I don't know. Should we still attack, sir?"
He sniffs the air. "Could be an ambush. No matter. The villagers are only postponing the inevitable."
"We have nothing to fear, so long as we have the jahk with us. Come, brothers. Let's see what's left for us here."

He scans the village for some time without speaking. He checks his belt where the horn should be a number of times.

Finally, he turns to look at the First, who moves her head from left to right. Ledak's shoulders fall. "I've failed you, brothers," he said, with none of his conviction from before. "Come, we must leave the village to their fate."
You glance at Matkina, still in the arms of her captors. She smiles uncharacteristically, a bead of moisture on her cheek.

His eyes narrow. "You fool. You'll kill them all."

He looks back at the First, who moves her head just slightly from left to right. "Leave the village and the traitors," Ledak orders. Then he glares at you. "Their deaths will be on *your* head."
"There will be *no* deaths today."
"Let me worry about that."
Let them go.
"Leave them to their fate."
"I'm not going to use it. Call off the attack, Ledak."
"More outsiders. Many, by the sound of it. Are you among them, Matkina?"
"They have me, yes." Matkina hangs her head. "Neng, I'm... I'm sorry."
"You have nothing to apologize for, child. You never have."
He sniffs the air then inexplicably faces you directly. "So. You prepare us for their coming, then stand with our attackers. What is the meaning of this, Outsider?"
He sniffs the air then inexplicably faces you directly. "You lied to us about when they would arrive. What is the meaning of this, Outsider?"
He sniffs the air then inexplicably faces you directly. "So now you stand with our attackers. What is the meaning of this, Outsider?"
Let Ledak speak.
"It would be better if you surrender, Neng."
"Don't worry, Neng. I'm on your side."
"Really?" Ledak chuckles softly as he draws his weapon. "Very well."
"What?! But I gave you the honor of..." He trails off as understanding dawns. His eyes fall to the jahk that you now carry.
"Call off the attack, Ledak."
[Attack] "For Kholn Village!"
"Turn back, Ledak. We don't have to do this."
Show Ledak the jahk. "Call off the attack, Ledak."
"What?" He reaches for the horn that is no longer at his side. "When did you...?"
"If that is what you came for, then draw your weapons now, for it will not happen."
"People of Kholn Village, you are not as safe as you think. The teratomorph attacks in the area *have* been traced to you, and not just by us. The Sand Knights plan to attack you at dawn."
Neng's dead eyes grow wide. "Is this true?"
"As surely as I stand before you. Your only hope is to give the teratomorphs among you to us. Serve the First, and she will keep you safe."
The old man's lips form a grim line. "You suggest slavery. Sand Knights or no, our people will die before we live in captivity."
"We're wasting our time, Colonel. He won't listen."
"There's no other way, Neng. You must surrender."
"He has the jahk. It will make it impossible for you to fight."
"We have the jahk. It will make it impossible for you to fight."
Say nothing.
He takes a deep breath. "Even so."
"Death first, *Outsider*."
"So be it. Brothers, take as many prisoner as you can." He lowers his voice. "Kill the rest."
Attack.
[Attack] "I'm sorry, Neng."
"For the First!"
"It's good you warned us of this," Ledak whispers.
"What?!"

Ledak places a heavy hand on your shoulder. "You have done well, Gerave. Glory in your victory this day."
"Obviously. Forgive me for doubting you. Well, rest assured that even an ambush won't save them today."
The villagers are not as prepared as they might be because they didn't know the attack was coming before dawn.
The villagers knew the attack was coming before dawn and so most of them evacuated. Only a few such as Neng stayed behind to give the others a chance to escape.

The villagers knew the attack was coming before dawn and so are able to put up a stronger defense than they would have otherwise.

This ancient door looks like it hasn't been opened in millennia.
It's older than anything you can see in the village.
And its age and style are different even than the buried structure the village is built on.
There are no visible seams or hinges, like it was never meant to be opened at all.
The paintings seem to dance across the rock face. You can make out people and strange creatures, but there seems no rhyme or reason to the pictures or their movement.
Matkina raises an eyebrow. "It's a story. I can't believe I didn't see it before."
"What do you mean?"
"Obviously it's a story, but of what?"
Examine the drawings.
Leave the drawings.
The drawings shift around in two obvious groups: one on a kind of map, and the other permeated with circular runes. All of it is framed in a kind of scribbled writing.
Examine the map and its related drawings.
Examine the drawings permeated with runes.

"I grew up in this village. When I was little, I'd come up here to be alone and play with the paintings. I never thought about how they connected to each other."

"But look, the islands and clouds are common settings. The deity, the herald, and the warrior are the protagonists in almost every scene. I'm *sure* it's a story. Touch them and see."
She shrugs. "I have no idea."
"What's the story about?"
The map is made up of three designs surrounding a number of islands. The designs and the islands pulse with a golden light. You feel like they're waiting for you to do something.
The runes are circular and flowing. they weave in and out of four figures, each of which pulse with a golden light like they're waiting for something.
Touch the group of islands.
Look at the other group, with the circular runes.
Touch the herald wielding a blade.
Touch the image of the deity, the herald, and the warrior standing in a line.
Touch the image of the deity, the herald, and the warrior locked in combat.
Look at the other group, with the map.

The map shifts and spins. The islands grow to take up the whole space, big enough that you think they might represent continents or even moons. Lush trees sprout from each one, and falls of water - or maybe roots - plunge off the sides. The glowing man looms large in the center like some kind of deity.

The deity raises his hands. Out of each of the islands arises a number of smaller beings. The people vary in color and appearance, some with tails or extra arms and eyes. All of them turn to the deity and raise their hands to him, palms outward. You guess the gesture is a kind of worship.

The deity then ascends above the islands and disappears.
Matkina huffs in annoyance.
"What is it?"
"These creation myths are all the same. Some god makes people he doesn't care about. They look up to him, then he abandons them. Why make them in the first place?"
"If he's a god, maybe he has reasons we don't understand."
"Maybe by leaving, it forces the people to grow stronger."
"It's just a myth. You're reading too much into it."
"It's just trying to make sense of life. To find meaning."
"Are you mad because they were abandoned or you were?"
She frowns. "Maybe."
"Are we done here yet?"
"Hmph. What good's a god who isn't there?"
"What a stupid reason to paint a story."
She gives you a sidelong glance.

The scene shifts toward the smaller beings working on the islands. The clouded area with the giant, glowing deity fades and disappears.

Slowly, gradually, the scene darkens, the people hunch over as they work, until most of them become the wild animal you first touched. One by one, they cease working and wander off aimlessly, or else attack each other, like beasts.

One of the smaller beings, shaded in violet, remains unchanged, though all around her the others have become wild creatures. She bears a horn, giving the impression that she's some kind of herald.

The herald falls to her knees and pleads to the sky. Then she rises up to the clouds where the deity sits, but the deity ignores her. She pleads and begs, but the deity casts her back to the islands.

The glowing deity casts the herald down to the islands.

The herald takes up a twisted blade and goes to the wild creatures around her. As she touches each one, the creatures turn back into small beings like the herald herself - colored differently, or with more arms or fewer eyes, but definitely beings of the same sort.

The herald leads this host to the clouds where the deity waits.

There is a great battle, but the deity is too powerful. He flings them back to the islands with great sweeps of his hand. Some of those struck stand up, albeit slowly. Many more do not stand up at all.
From the corner of your eye, you notice Matkina is trembling. "Nothing," she says. "It's nothing."
"You're trembling."

She hesitates, then shakes her head. "It's stupid, but... I feel like the herald is me and the deity is *him*, the so-called Changing God.

"I left this village a long time ago to take on our father, but now, in this village... what if everyone I care about is destroyed in the process?"
"It's not your fault."
"It won't happen. We'll stop it."
"It was worth the risk to you once."
"You don't know that." She scowls, and you swear you see a tear go back *into* her eye. "It doesn't matter. Whatever happens, I won't let *her* hurt these villagers."
"You're right. Whatever happens, I won't let *her* hurt these people."
She shakes her head again. "It wasn't a risk before. Now that it is... No, it's not worth it. Whatever happens, I won't let *her* hurt these people."

Smaller beings on the islands struggle to their feet. The herald goes to them, pointing at the clouds with her blade, apparently urging them to face the deity.

A green warrior with four-arms picks up his own blade and points it at the herald instead.

The herald rises to the clouds, twisted blade in hand.

The deity in the clouds has his back to the herald, unprepared for this second attack. The herald, likewise, does not see the four-armed warrior who has followed her to the clouds with his own host.

There is a great battle in the clouds above the islands. The herald fights the deity. The four-armed warrior and his host attack the herald, and the deity faces them both.

One by one, the hosts of the herald and the warrior are sent crashing to the islands. None stand back up.

The battle continues until only the deity, the herald, and the warrior remain. All others are dead on the islands, but these three remain locked in combat until the scene fades and the original designs return.

As the scene plays, a humming grows from within the wall. You feel a sucking sensation and suddenly the world goes black.

In the darkness, you hear Matkina mutter, "I'll be damned."

But it looks as though that function needs to be activated somehow before it will work. Possibly deciphering the writing will help with that.

"I think these pictures do something. I just need to figure it out."

"I just wanted to see the story. Let me try to activate it like Tik showed us."
"Who's the superior officer here? We'll go when I'm ready."
"Ugh, finally."
She crosses her arms. "Fine."

"You realize nobody's ever made them do anything, right? These paintings have been here for thousands, maybe hundreds of thousands, of years. They probably don't do anything at all. But if we don't leave soon, Ledak's going to ask dangerous questions."
"Just a little longer. I feel like I'm close to something."

"*I offer oblivion. Not everlasting torment. Not punishment. I offer your immortal companion the death it has always dreamed of,*" the Sorrow says simply.

Its eyeless gaze rests on Oom. "*I offer peace,*" it says softly.

Oom eyes the towering being for a moment. 

::smsssr:: it whispers at last, and returns to your side.
::sssslk:: Oom murmurs, gently turning from you. You feel the mental link between you - already damaged by your careless treatment of the creature - snap in half.

Oom hesitates, eyes contracting. 

::sssrl:: it hisses, shuddering. Unconvinced.
"We stood together in the ruins of your world, Oom. The Sorrow did that. Don't give up. Stay with *me*."

::rrrss:: Oom whispers to itself. ::srrrlk::

Eyes flicking between you and the Sorrow, it returns to your side, and wraps a careful tendril around your ankle. 

Oom growls long and low at the towering creature. You hear - and feel - a *rutch* within Oom and your own mind. Something, somewhere, has broken in the toy.

::srrrlll:: Oom growls, eyes widening - not in fear, but in rage, throbbing inside you like a second heart. It shrieks wordlessly at the Sorrow, and the sound rips the mental link to you - already damaged by your careless treatment of the creature - utterly asunder.

The Sorrow nods. 

"*Your companion has decided its fate. Let us return to our discussion of yours... and of the harm your kind has done to the Tides.*"
Oom strokes your ankle gently, one last time. Then, it turns towards the towering being opposite you.
Dark tendrils close around your tiny companion and Oom is gone. Nothing remains but dying motes of light the color of Oom's eyes, drifting into the air.

Armor's weight means little to you. While others rattle and stumble, you move through battle with calm assurance.

A little extra force is sometimes all it takes to succeed at certain physical tasks.
Your keen eye and your unerring strikes drive your foes to their knees.
You know how to place your feet, how to angle your shield, and how to deflect your enemies' blows. You dance through combat, and none can lay a finger on you.

Jokes about heritage, parentage, appearance, smell, and imagined mating habits leave your friends rolling with laughter, and your foes seething with rage. They will try to kill you for these slights, to the exclusion of all others, because of your mastery of the form.
A chain, a hook, and an unbalanced enemy - that's all you need to ruin someone's day.  You throw a chain around your target and drag your foe stumbling within range of your attacks.
They might be bigger than you. They might be stronger than you. But they're not as devious as you, and you prove it every time you face someone who tries to get the upper hand.
Obstacles? No problem. Especially if those obstacles are made of flesh. You're a natural with ranged weapons, and you know just where to aim to pick off the people who hide behind their allies.
Sometimes you might find yourself surrounded and realize that precision fighting isn't the best route forward. Sometimes only brute strength serves. Show them the error of their ways.
Make them notice you. Enrage your enemies and serve as the focal point of the battle.
You're never surrounded. You're exactly where you're supposed to be.
You're not done yet. After killing an enemy, you can turn your fury on another target without pausing for breath.
You strike the ground, unleashing a punishing wave of kinetic force that hurls your opponents away from you and knocks them down.
A foe can't fight if she can't move. Your opportunistic attacks shock your enemies' minds, stopping them in their tracks.
Focus. Effort. Precision. These are your watchwords, and you put them into play every time you make an attack.
You know how to make the most of  your body, and how to summon your deepest reserves. You can push yourself harder and longer than any but the most elite athletes.
Your mercurial temperament can occasionally be a hindrance... but when you focus on a skill, you are without parallel.
Blindfolded and upside down, you'd still hit your target. You're just that good.
Who needs armor? It's slow and cumbersome, and that extra weight might just get you killed. You prefer speed and mobility anyway.
You snap your fingers, and knots untangle themselves. Doors pop open.  Chests unlock. It's easy if you know how to do it.
Why fight fair? Take advantage of your opponents whenever you can - you know they'd do the same to you if the situation were reversed.
You force energy into your weapon, filling it with esoteric power. It's the perfect antidote to an armored enemy.
You know how to handle your cyphers and how to store them properly.
Make an ally of someone who stands in your way. Tap into your secret powers and change their minds for them.
Focusing on a point in the battlefield, you summon a glowing, ethereal being that whispers in your opponents' ears, distracting them.

A place exists under space - a way to connect two points by folding the fabric of reality. By touching these points together, you can almost be in two places at once... and the resulting burst of energy slows your foes.
You're a jack of all trades, able to make connections between disparate tasks. Your broad base of knowledge makes it a snap to apply your skills to new situations.
You blow a dry handful of nano-spirits into the faces of your enemies. The tiny creatures swarm through their minds, exploding with tiny bursts of agonizing energy.
You coat your weapon with a venom of your own creation. When you strike an enemy, you spill worms into his blood. They devour their way to fresh air and return to you, bringing the gift of life.
You don't get tired as easily as normal beings, and you're able to keep working on certain tasks when others would falter.
The best time to strike an enemy is when he's weakened.
You summon the energy from the very air around you, drawing strength and power in massive quantities... and then you release it in a great wave.
Assail your foes' bodies or their minds with a blast of summoned energy.
While speaking with the inhabitants of the Ninth World, you will sometimes hear their thoughts. This is often helpful, though rarely appreciated.
Channel a subtle esotery through the body of an ally, purging most negative effects from them and healing their wounds.
Surround your allies with a cloud of nano-spirits that will defend them against damage.
Distance is an illusion. You can manipulate space to create a shadow door, and draw your ally through it to the other side.
Your mind is an impenetrable tower of iron will, a fortress few can breach.
The knowledge of the ancients is at your fingertips. With a little concentration, you can summon esoteric lore and random trivia.
A mechanical enhancement to your biological eye helps you focus your more esoteric attacks.
Turn the mysterious forces of the world to your advantage. Fill your friends with power and your enemies with regret.
You create an explosion of energy with your mind, a swirl of power that bursts among your foes.
You create an energy-siphoning vortex, weakening all within its radius. None can stand before you.
Your unrivaled mental prowess strengthens your esoteries beyond the capabilities of weaker beings.
You create a temporary matrix in your corneas that highlight and sharpen details that might have otherwise remained hidden.
You focus on an ally, sharpening their reflexes and boosting their reaction times with your formidable psychic strength.
You treat one of the fundamental forces of the universe as a tool. You draw enemies into your orbit or send them reeling away with the power of your mind alone.
When you strike true, your enemies quail. The damage you do lasts beyond the moment, devouring your foes' energies from the inside.
You call upon hidden forces for aid. They shape a mindless minion from your desire and bind it to your will.
You seize control of a rival's nervous system and make her dance to your need. You spill discord among your foes, turning their strengths to horrible weakness.
You unleash a many-faceted assault upon all enemies before you, using every secret in your extensive repertoire.
He might be a drunkard, but Artaglio brings decades of tactical experience to every battle he fights... and now he's sharing that knowledge with you.
When you have a captive machine intelligence augmenting your mind, pattern-matching and memory-related tasks become so much easier.
You have given Choi a peace of sorts. She returns the favor, helping you endure through difficult and painful times.
Thanks to Erritis, your attacks are slightly more heroic now.
Your brother's agony and power lives within you, crippling you. Strengthening you.
The creature's alien thoughts fill your mind, lashing out at those foolish enough to attack you.
Seria's calming music fills you, strengthening you in every way.
You are a natural leader, a gracious speaker, and gifted with words. People find it easy to relate to you.
You have a keen eye for a bargain. Shopkeepers dread your coming.
Your steady leadership and ability to keep calm in danger is contagious. Your friends and allies can count on you to guide them to victory.
You are a thundercloud in your enemies' minds. Your presence looms in their thoughts, and they fear to cross your path for fear of the outcome.
You like people, and you especially like bringing them around to your point of view. It's refreshing and fulfilling.
You strike from the shadows. You see weakness in your enemies, and you strike *first* and hardest.
The darkness is your ally. You excel at skills suited for the shadows.
Your weapons blur between multiple dimensions, doing damage to armor, flesh, and reality itself.
None can prepare themselves for your vicious ambush. You leap from the shadows to deliver a devastating surprise attack.
Reality bends to your will, hiding you and your actions from your enemies.
In your skilled hands, you can make almost *anything* a shield.
You are a patient fighter, willing to wait until the moment is right to strike. Your rivals mistake this for fear... and when they test you, you show them why they were wrong.
Your hidden reserves keep you going when others would be spent.
Your armor fits you like a second skin. If it were up to you, you'd never take it off.
You withdraw to keep a watchful eye over the battlefield, and step in swiftly to take the blows meant for an ally.
Subconscious telekinetic energies coil about your body, driving back anyone foolish enough to lay hands on you.
When one exists in all realities, moving from *here* to *there* while avoiding an enemy's clumsy blows is simply a matter of willpower.

Callistege's sisters lend extra power to her attacks while she fluctuates between multiple realities.

Tybir shouts a series of sharp-tongued remarks on the appearance and parentage of nearby enemies, drawing their full and furious attention.

Tybir's seen a few things in his life, and he's more than willing to share what he knows. His allies benefit from his experience and eagerness to rehearse his favorite stories.
The Ninth World is full of the graves of honorable men, and Tybir has no intention of joining them. His attacks do much more damage against unprepared opponents.
One-on-one duels are not Erritis's style. He's far more effective leaping from enemy to enemy, dealing deadly wounds, and giggling beneath his breath.
Subtlety isn't very heroic. Smashing things is. By following Erritis's heroic example, all party members are much better at breaking things into small, cowardly pieces.
Erritis is stronger and faster than other heroes. Than *any* heroes, really. After all, he's the greatest hero who ever lived!
When Erritis lands a powerful blow, his aura flares, blinding his enemies and giving them a moment to consider how outmatched they really are.
With every powerful blow, Erritis's glow intensifies, and his attacks get stronger... and stronger... and *stronger*.
Rhin claims to have a god who knows everything of hiding. It's hard to argue with the results.
Whether Rhin's god of hiding is real or not, even her friends seem to benefit from being near her.
Rhin is always learning and asking questions. Her hunger for knowledge makes her more adept with cyphers than some natives of this strange place.
Bent wire, pieces of string, and a little help from one of her gods - so she says - make some of the cyphers Rhin uses last just a little bit longer.
Rhin has brought new gods back with her - terrifying gods who will tear apart anyone who dares harm her friends.
Ahl has grown to know more than just hiding. Rhin can call on his power to surround her allies with a healing light.
Varlin sleeps like a dull shin in Rhin's pocket, providing quiet but effective aid to Rhin and her friends.

"What is, was. What was, will be. What will be, was and will be again. RIP."
"Lightly repetitive in life, lightly repetitive in death."
"He sleeps. It happened simply, as naturally as the night falls when the day goes away."
"Denizen of the hidden planet, prince, and slayer of those who would cheat death."
"Through service, death. Through death, life."
"Looks like I died again, but I will find a way back, once more. One does not easily dispose of the Cleric."
"Dangerous and deadly throughout his warrior life until insanity ultimately slid him 6 feet under the soil. His signature grin is no less nefarious, even from the grave."
"'What can change the nature of a man?'\n'What does one life matter?'\nAn Aeon Priest may know, or learn, and share. With hours and days and lifetimes of dedicated research..."
"I found love in a hopeless place, and it killed me."

"Many live, and many create, but the beauty of destruction, few appreciate. The stoic living and venerated dead, offer truth? No, they beguile instead. Those truly alive embrace strife as bread, and claim their reward - never one of the dead."
There are faint scratches at the base of the monument which read, "For the Sergeant. We and our kin are yours to lead. Wherever, Whenever. -336th"
"It is amazing how much power one has in the universe if you just listen."
"For he was the one who brought with him the joy of sharing. For without him the many lives shared would never have been lost, as they never would have begun."
"This Jack jacked a pneumatic jack to jack a gemstack,\nBut attacked a stacked deck and got the Spade."

"Did not like mountains, will haunt you if buried in one.\nIn fact, she was the kind of tenacious woman that might just haunt you for reading this.\nIf haunted, try to destroy a mountain to soothe her."
"Love conquers fear."
"There is no pleasure without pain."

"The tides of time have come for me, have those in life forsaken me?
Will you drink to me, or will I remain amongst the forgotten?

His ladies live on, creating their own legends. 
Evelyn & Isabelle.
May their journeys be blessed & happiness long."
"I built a legacy. I thought it would give me comfort in the end. Now I see that it died with me."
"It was tough being me!"
"Teach yourself about the numenera. Skip the Aeon Priest part."
"I am who I am."
"Don't mind me"

"Forgive. Forget.
The past remains.
Hidden. Within.
You aren't insane.

Remember."
"Saw Everything. Said Nothing. Knowledge is there for those who seek."
"Never to be trusted with trivial things, for it was only great challenges at which he excelled."
"Never tell me the odds."
Someone has roughly scrawled something into the corner of this monument. "TBD"

"What a to-do to die today at a minute or two to two. A thing distinctly hard to say but harder still to do. For they'll beat a tattoo at twenty to two a ratatatat a tatatatoo and the dragon will come when he hears the drum, at a minute or two to two."
"We're not sure what he was thinking, but he certainly though about it a lot."
"Live every day like it's your last - it really helps sell it when you mutter your final words, 'Excellent. Everything is going according to plan.'"
"Every step is but the first one many paths."
"An epitaph like this is the price you pay for waiting too long."
"To pass was not a choice but 'tis the fate I have succumbed.\nI have faced so many trials; the worst is yet to come.\nWhat deeds I have accomplished here will surely be undone."

"With enough expenditure of persistence and will, there is almost no victory that cannot be bought.\nBut foolish is the one who knows not the cost of this victory in advance, nor considers their willingness to pay that price..."
"In this grand journey, I was as you are. You will be as I am."
"You will bear the burden of the world upon your shoulders no longer. But oh, how you will be missed and loved until the day you are joined."
Someone appears to have carved a lewd picture here.
"I was sure that I would never find happiness. I was right."

"Once there was a Rockman, crafting stories in the lands
Once they etched in a poem, the poet one of their fans
But not all were pleased, the decision triggered some whine
The Rockman's heart caved in, unable to hold the line."

"Guni the Ceturl Prince, beloved of his friends and subjects. The line between human and ceturl is broad, but Guni crossed it without hesitation or remorse, and earned the allegiance of a new people for his bravery."
"They said, 'Don't forget your towel... I forget it! Skist!'"
"I came here without being consulted and leave without my consent."
"Was certain that Golthiar Wrestling was the next big thing. It was not."
There is only a name written on this epitaph, but you can't tell if it was originally there or added later.
"He was here just a minute ago."
"His friends were machines, their whispers, scripture. His own friends he made, by their machine hands betrayed."

"The room was dark
Her lantern slip't
A grush soon put her
In the crypt"

"Seek the unseekable in the mist of cold,
The eternal truth has not yet been told.
Shatter the mirrors of your mind and soul,
Unfold the journey, beyond the Death's howl."

"He was a counselor to all the great leaders of the world. Sought out by many and provided sage advice to avoid war and conflict. He was killed while seeking to quell a war between warring nations. His last thoughts were of his baby girl, Auriel."
"Spent his life acquiring things and running from his past. Then he acquired synthsteel boots, which slowed him down just a bit too much."
"Alas, the halls of the dead are filled with mead and beautiful women. I should have come here sooner!"
"All the good we do will be for nothing unless others are willing to do the same."
"I lived as well as I could. As brave as I wanted. Saw many things, but kept my nature intact. It isn't hard to live. Being human is the real challenge."
"Never let it be said that I was bereft of virtue, even if I never fully understood how to live by it."
"Here lies a fallen Hero of the North, Draegor of Prince Valley. He died peacefully in his sleep, unlike the rest of his passengers."
"Consult your medicus."
"Doing the right thing only gets you killed. Or worse..."
"The fate I made was the only fate I deserved."
"Look ma, no hands!"
"His final words assured his mother that he could have been a competitor."

"Demonbane, Kinderblight, Godslayer, Dark Dragon. He shall be remembered for deeds great and terrible, forever changing the Ninth World in ways never seen before or since. May he find peace in retirement, beyond our reach, at home under the stars."
"The Ninth World Will Remember."
"A fighter to the end, but hopefully met it in peace. She will be missed by many, but will not be forgotten."
"Within each seed, there is a promise of a flower, and within each death, no matter how small, there's always a new life. A new beginning."

"Life only ends when influence does. But culture is as ruthless as nature. A long life, filled with fever and fervor, now just shivers and scrawls. But as futile as heat is, cold surrender is folly. Choose carefully who and what you heat, friend."
"I lived as I died. Badly.\n\nLearn from those around you to live your life the best that you can."

"Our last breaths in this tomb,
at last we are free.
Our two hearts afloat in rivers of time, finally beyond this reality.
Our two souls released,
like birds they fly away.
Finally together for all eternity."
"How high that highest candle lights the dark."
"In honor of nearly 100,000 souls who gave willingly and bravely to this world. It is a monument carved from their torment, from their dreams to yours."

The castoffs of Miel Avest are led by a woman named Aadiriis, a visionary who keeps the peace, forcing the castoffs to focus on finding ways to fight the Sorrow. Aadiriis possesses an uncanny beauty. She is a mother and guide to the castoffs, with a kind and caring demeanor, but a mortal threat to anyone who threatens the castoff sanctuary.

These transdimensional entities look like shadowy reflections of an angular, toothy humanoid, and the common folk believe them to be ghosts. They can phase in and out of reality at will, and they seek sources of transdimensional energy to feed upon. Beyond that, their motives are uncertain.

A dour explorer and former Aeon Priest, with living, intricately designed tattoos that writhe across his forearms, Aligern thinks you might be the Changing God. He is watching you closely. He can pull the tattoos from his arm as if they were wires under his skin, using them in battle to defend himself and his companions.

He wears a faded grey duster that buttons from the neck down to the waist. It has a number of pockets, bulging with small pieces of equipment.

These bipedal herd animals are common pack and riding animals. Their small forelimbs and tiny claws keep them from being much of a threat to their handlers, and their generally docile natures make them ideal for long journeys – even across worlds and through the Maws of the Bloom.

Artaglio is a deserter in one of the armies of the Endless Battle. A former captain, he and his mercenary company – Artaglio's Irregulars – make their camp in Chiurgeon Slump, a fetid slum in a fleshy pocket of the Bloom. Artaglio wears blue and silver finery and keeps his breastplate and weaponry shiny and well-polished. He is always accompanied by his men, including his former sergeant, Ranard.

Bericael Brunna is a warrior of iron will and exceptional self-control. Bericael is of indeterminate gender, and is muscular, slim, and tall. An unyielding foe, faithful ally, and deadly in battle, Bericael has been a squad leader and commando in the First's Militia for years and has been integral in many successful operations.

Only the most wretched and unfortunate people become permanent residents of the Bloom. Some are exiles, criminals, or madmen who were forced to flee the city of Sagus Cliffs. Others are vagrants with nowhere else to go. A few came here from far away – stumbling into a portal, perhaps – and found themselves trapped in the Bloom, with no hope of making their way back home. Eventually, the Bloom will devour them all.

Some people claim to know the ways of the Bloom. They've learned its tubes and byways, explored its stinking slums, and discovered what its Maws like to eat. Some even say that the Bloom favors them, opening passageways to take them where they want to go. Such people often hire themselves out as Bloom-guides, earning money by providing advice and direction to merchants and explorers. Their careers rarely last long, of course – the Bloom's favor is almost always short-lived.

Bloom-slaves are former criminals and convicts from the city of Sagus Cliffs. To pay their debt to society, some choose Bloom-slavery instead of prison or execution. They are auctioned off to merchants and explorers who use them to open the Bloom's Maws. Once a Bloom-slave has been fed to a Maw, they are free... that is, assuming they are still alive and mostly intact.

Bloom-tongues are wriggling tendrils that sprout from the flesh of the Bloom. Usually they surround Maws, but sometimes clusters of tongues exist on their own, especially in the deeper chambers of the Bloom. If you draw too near to a mass of Bloom-tongues, their voices will intrude upon your mind.

Beneath the crag of Sagus Cliffs, far below the level of human habitation, is a void in the rock. In the remote past, this place was a crossroads in some predecessor city, built by alien hands. More recently, the Changing God seems to have discovered this place and turned it into a secret refuge or laboratory. Inexplicably, the chamber is filled with breathable air, probably supplied by one of the Changing God's devices.

Callistege is a woman whose consciousness has fractured itself through the dimensions. Her echoes shimmer through multiple realities. She refers to these alternative shadows as her ""sisters"". She is a brilliant nano, and she seems to want something from you.

Callistege wears a bright wardrobe of oranges and reds, as if she were on fire. Her long, metallic hair shimmers. She wears earrings, necklaces, bracelets, anklets, and belts of varying materials and workmanship.

The highest peak of Sagus Cliffs serves as a mooring point for airships of all varieties, serving those who wish to avoid the dangerous overland journey to the Oasis of M'ra Jolios, the Valley of Dead Heroes, the city of Haref, or more distant destinations. A woman named Tranquility operates a hostel here for those who need a place to rest their heads.

Those who have been birthed by the Changing God's abandonment are known as castoffs. Though it's speculated that a few hundred or more are scattered throughout Sagus Cliffs and the wider Protectorate, no one knows how many there are.

For hundreds of years, the Cave of Last Words was a thieves' bolt-hole, a place for the criminal element to hide from the law. It was also the site of countless suicides, where desperate people spent their last moments before throwing themselves into the sea. A great many of them chose to leave their final thoughts on the walls – words of despair, introspection, and rage. The Cave has, of late, been your sister Matkina's home as she sank deeper and deeper into paranoia and dementia.

Legends say that Chila was a teenage girl from Sagus Cliffs, forced into slavery in the Bloom. She formed a unique bond with the Bloom, and used that bond to start a slave rebellion that ultimately spilled into Sagus Cliffs. The slaves brought down the city's government and toppled its empire, installing Chila as their autarch. Ever since, Sagus Cliffs has been governed by those who trace their lineage to Chila's slave companions. Statues of Chila depict her with silver skin and a massive war hammer.

Worshippers of your castoff brother Inifere, the Children of the Endless Gate are a splinter sect of the Dendra O'hur. They seek to "free" the spirits of the living from the prisons of their bodies. The Children use the blood of their victims to draw the symbol of the Endless Gate. If the Gate opens, the cultists hurl their screaming victims into the nightmare beyond. The Children pray to the entity within the Endless Gate in the hope that it will calm the turmoil in their own lives – or that it will grant them its power.

This little pocket of Bloom-flesh has attracted a small collection of quacksalvers and chiurgeons, most of whom are here because of various ethical violations or ugly obsessions. The place is now under the command of a band of deserters from the Endless Battle, Artaglio's Irregulars.

The Church of the Changing God – at least its Sagus Cliffs chapter – venerate the Changing God as a literal deity, a man who has transcended mortality. They view castoffs as facets of his godhood. Its followers study the Changing God's exploits and seek to gain a deeper understanding of his actions so that they can apply his lessons to their lives. He is a symbol of enlightenment and knowledge to them, and they believe that by emulating him, they can heal the Ninth World of its ills.

One of the prime markets in Sagus Cliffs, Circus Minor plays host to all manner of itinerant merchants and city spectacles. At its heart stands the Clock, the machine once said to have unmoored the city in time during an invasion. All manner of public events happen here – traveling religious revivals, executions, performances, and more. It sits near the bottom of the city, very near the Reef of Fallen Worlds.

This tough neighborhood sits along one of the more exposed faces of Sagus Cliffs. Sagging houses line the steep road – some along the cliff itself, where the ground is slowly crumbling away beneath them. This area is home to lower-class citizens, as well as merchants, beggars, and grifters. It also features a chiurgical parlor and the Fifth Eye tavern.

Sometimes the Bloom's Maws break free of its body and fragment into smaller, autonomous creatures. These ravenous horrors are known as corpuscular maws. They consist of a small central core, containing a tiny portal to another time or place, surrounded by knots of Bloom-flesh that form into arms and tendrils. The "arms" serve as a means of locomotion as well as attack.

Crystalvores are insectoid beings of unknown origin. They generate a chemical process that dissolves crystal, using it to hollow out crystalline chunks to serve as shells. They use their sharp mandibles, talons, and claws to make short work of those who intrude on their nests. They frequently withdraw within their shells, falling into a dormant state until they are disturbed.

A decanted is a tall, white automaton with a frosted glass dome implanted in its chest. Inside the dome is a frozen human head. The construct speaks through a buzzing grill, its voice stripped of emotion. Decanted sometimes appear in groups, sometimes alone, usually seeking healthy and beautiful humans to bring back to their city of Glass.

The Dendra O'hur are worshippers of the Lady of Maggots, the Great Queen Sar'lavun. They are a cult of cannibals, devouring flesh to draw the memories of the dead into their own minds. They wear distinctive robes, draped with hoses and filters, that they use to reduce their meals into an easily digestible slurry.

Dracogen is a gray-skinned, sharp-toothed artifact dealer, obsessed with the wonders of the prior worlds. Though he's widely traveled, he calls the Bloom home for now. He has cultivated a reputation for fair dealing and complete ruthlessness toward those who cross him – and he always finds out when he’s been cheated.

Centuries ago, the Changing God and his castoffs worked together against the Sorrow. He and the First Castoff were especially close... until the day when a disagreement poisoned their relationship. The disagreement became an argument, which became a struggle, which became a battle and then a war. The castoffs chose sides, devoting their tremendous powers and talents to bloodshed. Some sided with the Changing God, believing that he had a plan to stop the Sorrow's genocide, or from a loyalty to the man responsible for their creation. Others sided with the First, believing that she had their best interests at heart against a fundamentally selfish creator. 

The two sides fought with all the weapons at their disposal, always to a draw, until the Changing God's armies suddenly began to suffer defeat after defeat. He discovered that his weapons were worthless, for the First had found the Reconciler of Truth, a device that could collapse multiple realities. He sought – and found – a counter in Heaven's Rejoinder, and the overlapping realities of their effects have torn time in the battlefield, parallel truths rolling and twining around each other. 

A century ago, the First sought to end the battle and strike a decisive blow against one of the Changing God's mercenary companies, the Sand Knights. Her lieutenant, Paj Rekken, was charged with leading an assault on one of the Sand Knights' fortresses, and she gained entry just as the First was torn apart in a coruscation of energies. Rekken did not know the First had been destroyed and used the Reconciler to snap the realities together, maintaining victory over the Sand Knights. By the time Rekken learned of the First's death, the First was irrevocably lost. The battle continues to divide the castoff community, and mercenaries still flock to the battlefield, but the Changing God has moved on.

A brash glaive, his intellect dimmed by the brilliant glow that surrounds him, Erritis is always ready for adventure – the more dangerous, the better! – and he's overjoyed to have you along to support him.

Erritis is an unusually attractive young man, and his guiding star is to have as much excitement in his life as possible. Erritis doesn't plan, he doesn't do "tactics," and he doesn't like thinking things through because, really, what has that ever done for anyone, anyway? Point him toward a catastrophe, and let him go! And if no catastrophe exists? Time to create one!

Those who worship the Bloom as a god are known as the Extremities of the Great Devourer. 

Their greatest desire is to achieve union with the Bloom. They want only to serve the Bloom, to be brought to its innermost heart. They wear the Bloom's flesh as clothing and wear no shoes, so that they can touch their god at all times. They believe that being devoured by the Bloom is a mark of their deity’s favor, and they actively seek to be eaten.

The powerful, amoral woman who called herself the First Castoff of the Changing God was once one of the primary allies of the Changing God... but she betrayed him, or claimed that he betrayed her, and she led a great castoff revolt against him – a revolt that has spanned centuries and still continues today. According to legend, she fell in battle against the Changing God, and once he had vanquished her, he quit the field.

Residing in the Underbelly's Manufactory are three large constructs. Millennia ago, these Foremen built and maintained massive starships. Though they can no longer move, they are still able to direct the efforts of human laborers. The Foremen are constantly devising better ways to fabricate materials and rework the numenera to benefit Sagus Cliffs.

Gar-koto is a prince among the mutants of Little Nihliesh, who revere those with the most severe mutations as nobility. He dwells inside a spherical tank, filled with murky fluid, making it impossible to catch more than a brief glimpse of his hideous form. The mutant prince speaks through a staticky grille at the front of his tank. He and his people have been stuck in the Bloom ever since the unexpected death of the Maw that led to their home city.

The Ghibra Ny'kul – the children of Ny'kul – are the native inhabitants of the Oasis of M'ra Jolios. They are a race of aquatic humanoids, varying widely in appearance. They believe that this physical diversity is a gift from their god. They may have scales, hide, or shells; flippers or legs; claws or fingers. 

The Ghibra communicate telepathically in a language they call Colosh Ny'kul – the word of Ny'kul. They frequently speak the Truth as well, for they believe in maintaining relationships with the world outside their watery bubble."

The Council of Sagus Cliffs meets on the sun-swept square at the top of the crag, overlooking the broad waters of Garravia Sound. Enormous synth slabs pave the square, and the tips of ancient space-faring vessels protrude from the ground, now repurposed as public buildings. The Order of Truth maintains its small, independent headquarters inside one of the starships, and emissaries from strange places meet in the Red Thicket, where their words cannot be overheard.

Imbitu is the elderly leader of the Dendra O'hur chapter in Sagus Cliffs. Friendly and cunning, Imbitu  is devoted to keeping human knowledge from the grasp of the Great Queen Sar'lavun, the Lady of Maggots, who waits on the other side of death to devour the minds of those who pass on. Imbitu has consumed the corpses of countless leaders and scholarchs, so he possesses the experience of many lifetimes.

Inifere is one of your castoff siblings, born in a dimension of horror. He is almost skeletal in appearance, and utterly mad. He would be harmless if it were not for the cultists who venerate him as the living portal to the Endless Gate.

Soldier-sailors in service to some long-vanished interstellar empire, the lascars appear to be human underneath their bulky, highly-polished armor. Their exotic weapons suggest that it would be unwise to antagonize them. Most of the lascars speak an unfamiliar language and carry themselves with a practiced, military bearing. A Maw opened in the Bloom, connecting the Ninth World to their "anchorage."

The constables of Sagus Cliffs are called levies – an army of nearly identical, manufactured humanoids who wear the silver-indigo colors of the city. It’s clear from the briefest of glances that levies are not quite human. Their features are plain, forgettable, and generic, their eyes too large, their smiles too firmly fixed on their faces. Though their manner is typically friendly, most people find them unsettling and try to avoid interacting with them.

Little Nihliesh is the trash heap of the Bloom, as if the Bloom used this cavity as some sort of filtering organ. It's the home to a collection of mutants led by Gar-koto, whose people live among the squalor and debris. The back end of the catena can be seen here, its opposite end protruding into the Memovira's Courtyard.

In the distant past, the anchorage was a lavish port for trade and tourism between worlds. Constructed in grand style, sparing no expense, it orbits a world that is far from your own. The civilization that built the anchorage is long gone, and the place is inhabited only by lascars, descended from those who once crewed the ships that came and went from the anchorage. Now they are trapped in the anchorage, maintaining its systems as best they can, awaiting a ship that will take them home.
Your castoff sister is an albino assassin feared across the Sagus Protectorate. They call her the White Death. She is a calculating jack of all trades, with a huge intellect and enormous potential.

The Maws of the Bloom appear as mouth-like orificies, surrounded by foul, questing tentacles called “tongues.” Each Maw harbors a singular desire – for instance, an emotion like hatred, human blood, or memories of happiness. Sating that desire will open a portal to some other place or time... whether within the Bloom, an alien world, or a new dimension.

Wires and tubes run through your brother Mazzof's body. He has a special affinity – an almost-spiritual connection – for machines. He was captured by the Ghibra during a raid on one of M'ra Jolios's treasure troves and was abandoned by his ally, the Changing God.

Melmoth Leviarm is the leader of the cannibalistic Dendra O'Hur, and is devoted to the idea of retaining knowledge in all its forms. He wears tattered leather robes draped with a profusion of wires and tubes. He has piercing eyes set amidst a hideously scarred face, and he wears tattered robes, with countless wires and tubes snaking from every corner of his body.

Melmoth is a master of the Tides, having spent his life trying to understand their function. He does not suffer fools lightly.

The Memorialists inhabit the Valley of Dead Heroes, tending the monuments and tombs. They teach that the Ninth World is the afterlife, and that the Valley contains the graves of every person on earth. They claim that if the "living" of the Ninth World find the graves of who they were in life, the Ninth World will become a true paradise. Conversely, if more of them forget their true selves, the world will slide into utter chaos. Thus the Memorialists maintain the graves, hoping the world will at last come to its senses.

The Memovira's Courtyard is an antechamber to the Bloom, and one of its main centers for human activity– it remains relatively stable, so people have built shanties and slave pits, the better to launch expeditions deeper in the Bloom. A catena crashed into the Bloom recently, and its leading car is here, slowly being absorbed into the Bloom's flesh. The Courtyard is adjoined to the Memovira's Fortress by a great gate, which is guarded at all times.

Miel Avest is a refuge from the Sorrow, a hidden sanctuary for castoffs alone, created by the Changing God and the First Castoff. Shields cast by generators from a long-dead world hide it from prying eyes. The only law in Miel Avest is peace, and in its verdant air castoffs can focus on ways to stop the Sorrow forever.

These birdlike abhumans are covered in greasy black feathers, their faces surmounted by sharp yellow beaks and beady eyes. They wear tattered leather cloaks and carry bulging leather bags to hoard the treasures they compulsively collect.

Mutants are humans whose bodies or minds are radically different from the norm. Sometimes these differences are due to the natural forces of evolution, and sometimes they are the result of an unnatural manipulation. In the Ninth World, mutants often band together, as those with hideous deformities may face violence and derision. While many mutants are outcasts, others are revered for the powers that their mutations confer upon them.

A nychthemeron is a hovering, biomechanical monstrosity, its squid-like body mounted atop a hovering orb, lasers and scalpels at its tentacles' tips. During the day, it is a creature of rage and hate. At night, it is calm and rational. Two explorers captured a nychthemeron, displaying it in a cage of energy in Circus Minor.

Oom is an amorphous blob that you found hiding in the mirrors of the Buried Crossroads. Once contacted, Oom made a home in your mind. It's clearly psychically reactive, and it seems to have bonded to you.

The Order of Truth stretches far across the Ninth World, though its philosophies and activities differ from place to place. Its primary goal is to use the tools of the vanished worlds to help restore humanity to greatness. Those who join the Order are called "Aeon Priests", though they are not a religion. Instead, they prize intellect, understanding, and a deep comprehension of the wonders of the ancient world. Across the world, people trust Aeon Priests to handle, identify, and use the numenera.

As commander of the First's Militia, your sibling Paj is devoted to the struggle against the Changing God. She now carries the First's mantle and has devoted centuries of her life to overthrowing your sire. Paj is utterly committed to the survival of the castoffs, and she has little patience for those who support the Changing God, who she says seeks to kill all of your kind.

The machine intelligence known as Peerless is more like a virus, installing copies of itself in other machines. These machines become Peerless drones, bloodthirsty and insane, and every one is convinced that it is the original Peerless. No one knows where the true source of the Peerless drones can be found.

Nowhere is the evidence of ancient civilizations more apparent than in the Reef of Fallen Worlds. In one section of the harbor, forgotten structures and abandoned war automatons break the surface of the water. This is prime pick for brave scavengers, but the place hides significant dangers for the unwary and the unlucky.

When a person you meet in the world has made a strong enough impression, a reflection of that person is born within the Calm of your mind. These are often distorted echoes of their true selves, but they might still hold secrets... or untapped power.

You found Rhin hiding from slavers in a pile of rubbish in Cliff's Edge. 

The poor child has a clearly visible head wound, and she says she came from another world. She claims to talk to gods and carries their totems in her pouch. Is she insane, or does she truly hold some latent power? Whatever her truth, she looks to you for her survival.

Sagus Cliffs is one of the oldest human cities in Greater Garravia, built upon the ruins of more ancient metropolises. It occupies the headland overlooking Garravia Sound, with switchbacks and cutouts in the bluffs creating broad avenues that wind down to the harbors. Humanity has filled the old streets with their own ramshackle constructions, building wherever they can find a place to stake their claim. Strange towers and remnants of lost worlds pock the city here and there, and old machines still hum in the artificial caverns beneath the city. It is in these caverns that you see the city's true geological strata – the detritus of forgotten times.  Some neighborhoods close to the cliffs' edges are in danger of falling into the bay below. Every year, the city loses a little ground and a few more lives.

Once the heart of the Sagus Protectorate, the city's fortunes have slipped, its territory shrinking to a small pocket of land surrounding the city.

The people of Sagus Cliffs are laborers, merchants, artisans, entertainers, bureaucrats, vagrants, and criminals. Many are descended from the first people who settled here almost a thousand years ago. They're quite accustomed to the weird artifacts that are scattered about their city, but they're wise enough to avoid them. At least, most of them are.

You found this young woman's corpse beneath the wreckage of a collapsed house in Cliff's Edge. When you first saw her, she dragged you into the Labyrinth of your mind, where she appeared as the shadowy outline of a woman. You found a puzzle box that was precious to her in life, allowing her to manifest as a ghost of her former self, but she is still just a memory... a reflection that belonged to another castoff.

Despite their name, silver orphans have little in common with helpless waifs. They are roughly the size of a full-grown human with shimmering, silver-alloy skin. They wander the Ninth World, seeking news of machine intelligences for some inexplicable reasons of their own. Silver orphans cannot speak, so they typically communicate through gestures and drawings.

Sir Arthour Torein is a traveler and one of the foremost experts on the numenera... at least, that's what he says. He makes his home in the Steadfast, and has one of the most extensive libraries about the numenera in the known world. He is always on the move, seeking to build upon his existing knowledge.

For centuries, the Slave Families have ruled Sagus Cliffs. They claim to be descended from the slaves who followed Chila the Great to victory over the old bosses of the city. The leaders of each family form the governing Council of the city, which seems simultaneously competent and disinterested in the affairs of the common people. Most members of the Council are content to wield power without drawing attention to themselves, but every rule has its exceptions. One such exception is Yars Vuntgen, a fat, yellow-skinned aristocrat who fancies himself a rabble-rouser.

Sticha are large, insectoid creatures. They are both organic and metallic, using their powerful digging claws to tunnel through rock. This activity generates piezoelectric energy that they feed upon. Sticha hatch from eggs and dig "death tunnels" when they are ready to die. They communicate via gestures, clicks and whistles, and a complex pheromonal language.

Before humanity emerged on earth about a thousand years ago, the Tabaht ruled Greater Garravia. They believed that conflict clarified them, and they thought of themselves as the perfect fighting force. Their chained god, an enslaved machine intelligence called the Underspine, guided them and prophesied their future. They claimed to be the chosen people of New Earth and destroyed any who dared stand against them. 

That is, until they met the humans at Sagus Cliffs. This defeat led to their ruin, and when a massive detonation destroyed the Underspine, the Tabaht were finished. Only the Genocide remains, the last remnant of a forgotten people.

Tash was a member of the First's Militia, tasked with retrieving the jahk from Kholn Village with Matkina, but you rewrote his history when you entered his Merecaster, restoring Matkina's memory in the process.

The Ascension of Kex-Lianish is a world of stark, crystalline beauty, located far from the Ninth World and accessible only through one of the Bloom's Maws. Lights flicker within the crystals, some of which have strange, intricate shapes. The Ascension's sun is small and distant, leaving it in a cold, perpetual twilight. Explorers and merchants occasionally venture here, but they are few, and rarely stay for long.

The people of the Steadfast call the lands outside their kingdoms "the Beyond" – but what they really mean are the lands west of the Clock of Kala, north of the Southern Wall, and south of the Caecilian Jungle. The communities of these places have their own laws, living independently of the Amber Pope.

The Bloom is an amoeboid leviathan the size of a city, hauling itself through a gorge near Sagus Cliffs, inch by inch, trying to reach the sea. Its tendrils anchor it to the valley's walls – but they also reach through time and dimensions. Where it anchors its tendrils, portals open to far-off places, and explorers who dwell within the Great Devourer rush to take advantage of the  distant worlds and dimensions it unlocks.

The Chalcedon is commander of the Changing God's forces in the Endless Battle. He is devoted to your creator, believing that the Changing God has a plan that will stop the Sorrow for good. He is a dangerous foe and a brilliant tactician.

The landscape, culture, and history of Sagus Cliffs have been shaped in innumerable ways by the Changing God. At one point in the distant past, he was a respected researcher and scientist, albeit flawed and selfish. But unlike most mere humans, the Changing God is not confined to a single lifetime.

For centuries, the Changing God has continued his existence by transferring his consciousness into bodies of his own creation, casting off the many vessels that have held his mind. He has moved from life to life, whether to avoid pain, injury, or death, or to seek new sensations and experiences. 

What he didn't realize – at first – was that the bodies he left behind, though often left severely damaged, were not empty. Each time he tore his mind from one of these husks, a new consciousness was born inside – a new person with their own thoughts and dreams.

The Ninth World contains realms of wonder and beauty – and places of utter, mind-destroying horror. The Endless Gate is one such place, a doorway that leads to a being of infinite hunger. Those with great psychic potential draw its attention. One such is the castoff Inifere, abandoned in the Endless Gate – and his travails have brought him worshippers who venerate the Gate's power. The Children of the Endless Gate seek to liberate their hellish master in exchange for a sliver of its unfathomable power.

The Fifth Eye is an abandoned pumping station from a prior world, now used as a tavern by the people of Sagus Cliffs. Pipes lead deep underground, pumping a variety of fluids into the tavern. No one knows what the fluids are, but after some experimentation, they've learned which ones are relatively harmless and capable of intoxicating people. Veterans of countless psychic wars share ownership of the Fifth Eye, and they remain here at all hours. Something about the Fifth Eye's architecture serves to drown out the constant mental noise of the city. Their shared mental strength attracts strange beings from across the universe.

You are the Last Castoff, a discarded shell built to hold the consciousness of the Changing God, a man obsessed with cheating death. You awoke within the dark fathom of your own mind after plummeting from orbit toward Sagus Cliffs. It is a miracle that you managed to survive... and as the Sorrow draws closer to you, you may not survive much longer.

The ruler of the Bloom is a crime lord known as the Memovira. The Memovira is not a name, but a title, and it has passed to many individuals throughout history. As such, not every Memovira rules the Bloom in the same manner, but they are all bonded to the Bloom, and lead only by its favor.

The countless dead of innumerable worlds find their eternal repose in the honeycombed cells of the Necropolis. Each civilization comes here through some strange compulsion, using the vast storage of the enormous cavern beneath the Valley to preserve the memories of their absent compatriots. No doubt one could spend years exploring the vaults.

The Ninth World is Earth, a world that has seen massive civilizations rise and fall over the course of two billion years since sentient life first arose – civilizations that could rekindle a dying sun, seed the atmosphere with nano-machines, shape the continents themselves into a massive mega-continent, become the seat of a vast interstellar empire, or make the fundamental forces of physics their playthings.

The caretaker at the Shrine of Great Chila is a small, elderly woman who calls herself the Observant Speck. Whenever she speaks, her words are softly echoed by the chittering voices of the Bloom, and she claims to understand what they are saying. She also claims to have met your sire, the Changing God, though that was many years ago. It's likely that she knows more about the Bloom and its secrets than anyone else alive.

The Sorrow is an ancient horror that hunts the Changing God and all his creations – namely, the castoffs. When you woke deep in the Labyrinth of your mind, you felt the Sorrow's inexorable pressure as you rebuilt your memories. When you emerged into the Calm and spoke to the Specter, the Sorrow ripped its way into your mind and spilled its fragments into your psyche.

A fragment of your imagination, the Specter manifests himself in the Calm. He is a handsome, affable man – or at least would be, if he weren't also a wispy, blue, psionic ghost. He drew power from the other memories that were in your mind to summon you back to consciousness, activating your body's healing abilities when you fell from the sky. He's a valuable friend - of sorts – and a font of information.

The Vast Interior is a cavernous void in the midst of the Bloom. Bony platforms cling to the walls or sit atop columns of flesh and gristle. Walkways connect these platforms, crafted by humans using whatever unpleasant materials are close at hand, suspended above the Bloom's cavernous depths. Some platforms hold shrines, shops, or homes, including the Shrine of Great Chila.
A charming rogue, a former mercenary, and an admitted confidence man – but not necessarily the bravest. He's quick with a blade, faster with his tongue, and prefers to lead from behind.

Far below the great ships that dominate Government Square lies the Underbelly, a series of caverns cut from the compressed detritus of millennia. Per its name and reputation, the dregs of society congregate in the gloom – mutants, the desperately poor, the cannibalistic Dendra O'hur, and other outcasts. The sticha can also be found here, digging and tunneling through the Underbelly's stone caverns.

Northeast of Sagus Cliffs, a pair of mountain ranges surrounds the Valley of Dead Heroes. The Valley is utterly lifeless, but it is filled with shrines, statues, and cenotaphs.  Many of these monuments were constructed by hands dead for millennia. Oddly, no corpses are buried in the valley – they are entombed in the Necropolis, which lies directly beneath the valley floor.

These humanoid creatures are tall and gaunt, with a violet-red tint to their flesh. Their eyes are contralateral and bulging, and a tall crest surmounts their head. They are often described by humans as cold and unemotional.

Waits-for-prey is an ancient construct created for battle. It is humanoid, but its entire body is lined with thorns and spikes, and its arms are long killing blades. Originally built by some vanished civilization from a prior world, it is now one of the last of its kind. Waits-for-prey has been standing in the Memovira's Courtyard for decades, accepting challenges from powerful people and creatures, and it has never been defeated.

Your mind is a strange place. The Changing God created some sort of psychic home for himself, a structure to contain his memories and consciousness. Reflections of people you once knew stand in the Calm at the center of your mind, and Fathoms below hide secrets and powers that your body once knew how to harness. Further exploration seems warranted... especially because the Sorrow has infected you with its fragments.

Far to the west of Sagus Cliffs, past the trackless wastes and the Clock of Kala, the nine nations of the Steadfast form a nucleus of civilization centered around the Amber Papacy – the core of the Order of Truth. The nine kingdoms of the Steadfast are Navarene, Milave, Ghan, Thaemor, Draolis, Malevich, Ancuan, Iscobal, and the Pytharon Empire.

While the Steadfast is settled and civilized, it is still a dangerous place. Isolated communities are still threatened, and travel is risky.

Aneen Meat

Essence of Violence

Essence of Bravery
