A well-used, carefully honed dagger. One of the simplest weapons available, but in the right hands also one of the most lethally quick.

Artaglio's Standard

Antique Hair Clip

This small, ornamental comb is actually a living, jeweled insect - a biomechanical marvel. The pincers seek to fasten themselves upon locks of hair, and its wings allow it to hover around the wearer's head, creating unique styles that would otherwise be impossible.

You acquired this letter of pardon from the Council Clerk. It grants a stay of execution for a criminal named Col Cardin, whose principal crime appears to have been treason. The paper is old and looks like it's been folded and passed hands many times, but it is certainly legitimate.
Nychthemeron Brain

This fusion of biological and mechanical parts apparently comprises the brain of a nychthemeron, its shape as alien as the creature itself. It was damaged somewhat during your fight with the creature - not to mention your grisly attempt to excise it from the body - but it seems to be mostly intact.
Notes on Nychthemeron
This sheaf of notes contains El-Jinto's observations and discoveries about the nychthemeron. He asked you to give them to Beleazar, an Aeon Priest.

This metallic object resembles a clenched, eight-fingered "hand" attached to a forearm. You snapped it off a metallic tendril in the Reef of Fallen Worlds. It has a decent heft and balance, and its steely material is powerful enough to deal significant damage, but it's only a makeshift weapon and is somewhat clumsy to use.

This hibernating fleshy worm has a disturbingly human face. Even holding it gives you a feeling of unease and weakness. Whispering a word to the worm will cause it to awaken. It can then be thrown at a living being, and it will attach itself to their flesh, releasing toxins into their bloodstream. These toxins cause instantaneous and powerful hallucinations, real enough to feel like memories to the victim. The hallucinations spin a tale of weakness, vivid enough to translate into actual vulnerability.
Ecstasy Glass

This device is made of six conjoined glass spheres. When used, the glass spheres take over the senses and flood the user with profound pleasure. The user cannot see, hear, smell, taste, or feel anything in the immediate surroundings during this time. Instead, the glass grants the experience of whatever is most desired, be it eating a sumptuous meal, engaging in a sexual act with one or more people she desires, or simply sitting comfortably in a beautiful landscape. This infuses the user with renewed energy, after which the glass spheres go dull and cannot be used again.

At first glance, this looks like an ordinary ring of minimal value. On further inspection, you find tiny sliding plates with indecipherable runes on the inside. When the ring is twisted in a certain way, the plates interlock, pulling the wearer out of phase with reality.​​

The contact points on this twisted metal cube are difficult to press with merely human hands. Once pressed, the device releases its time-manipulating powers. Because these powers were not tuned for human use, their effects are primarily mental invigoration.\n\nThese devices, called Standstills, have been used to infiltrate secure locations or for particularly difficult heists. Caution is advised: many have been known to fail the user at the time of greatest need.
Fiery Heart

This device is made up of two crystalline energy cells, charged almost to the point of detonation and then placed in two "chambers" inside a ceramic container. Throwing the container shatters the individual compartments, causing a powerful explosion.\n\nPutting your ear to the ceramic, you can hear a faint throbbing from the powered crystals.

Heavy and solid, this brown orb feels like a rock that has been worn smooth by a constant flow of water. On one side, there's an indentation that just fits a human hand. When activated, the bounder absorbs the user and teleports them to a nearby location within line of sight.

Scavenged from one of the machines in the strange laboratory where you attuned to the Tides, this stronglass globe crackles with brilliant energy stored inside. It could be manipulated to unleash the stored energy at an enemy.

You retrieved this curved metal rod after repairing one of the machines in the strange laboratory where you attuned to the Tides. It appears to be some kind of data tunneler, with exposed wires that previously attached to the machine. By crossing two of the exposed wires at once, it can be used for a single teleportation.

Shatterstar

This many-pointed star has a shimmering, bluish surface, highly polished to touch and sight. Though it appears at first glance to be crystal, it actually has a very fine mechanical structure. On the slightest impact, even a light tap of a finger, it shatters into many pieces and then immediately reforms.

This hibernating fleshy worm has a disturbingly human face. Even holding it gives you a feeling of unease and weakness. Whispering a word to the worm will cause it to awaken. It can then be thrown at a living being, and it will attach itself to their flesh, releasing toxins into their bloodstream. These toxins cause instantaneous and powerful hallucinations, real enough to feel like memories to the victim. The hallucinations spin a tale of weakness, vivid enough to translate into actual vulnerability.  [Lore: Mystical] The Call of the Inevitable were once a more common species, used by soothsayers and shamans in their rituals. As time passed, they were increasingly used as part of elaborate hoaxes until people discovered the truth and attempted to eradicate every last one of these worms. Very few are left now.  [Lore: Natural Science] The "call" of the worm is part of its procreation process, as its toxins contain tiny eggs that start their lives inside the person's system and are passed out to begin a new lifecycle for the species. Scholars believe the "call" is meant to make the carrier of the eggs more careful and thus more likely to survive.​
Bao

This rodent in a stronglass sphere was one of three that lived with Madelia Glittering. After misfortune struck Madelia, Bao agreed to travel with you.\n\nBao's precise nature, and the extent of her intelligence, are a mystery to you. Still, her nose twitches excitedly whenever you look at her, and you sense that she is enjoying her travels with you.
Interdimensional Puzzle Box

This is a small metallic cube, recovered from the ruins of a collapsed house in Cliff's Edge. It is etched with tiny symbols, but the means of opening the box is not obvious from a cursory visual inspection.
Zebb's Dad's Locket
Description of Zebb's Dad's Locket
This is a cluster of leathery-shelled eggs that you stole from the sticha lair. When you touch them, you can feel a tingle of electrical energy bound within.
Procreative Surge Turbine
This is a heavy metallic cylinder bristling with tubes and wires. Warm, smoky light pulses from within. It appears to be an energy transfer device, tuned for a very specific purpose.
Stillborn Construct

This inert little figure of metal and synth was cobbled together from parts of the Crippled Foreman, making it one of the construct's "children." With your help, the Foreman transferred some of its energy into the little creature, but for some reason it never came to life.
Stichus Egg
This stichus egg has been modified to serve as a power source. It is fitted with small, humming attachments and a prong that could be attached to another device.
Chronal Transference Device

This is a blinking and humming assembly of synth and metal parts, cobbled together from spare components of the machine that creates the levies of Sagus Cliffs. The device should transfer a single year of life from a human to his or her respective levy... assuming both parties are willing.
Avatrol Leather Jerkin

This simple garment is fashioned from the hide of an avatrol, a belligerent and spiteful beast that roams the Beyond in packs. Avatrols are immune to most energy attacks, and their skins retain a certain amount of this resistance after death, so avatrol leather is popular among hunters and explorers of the region. The tough material is also thick enough to offer a minimal amount of physical protection.
Cobbled Brigandine

This stout leather body armor is reinforced with small metal plates. It is heavier than a leather vest and provides more protection. Most of the metal plates are ordinary steel, but a few are made of more ancient and exotic materials, which imbue the armor with minimal protection against non-physical attacks. Spaces have been left between the plates so that the armor remains flexible, offering the wearer some freedom of movement.
Plate Armor

Individual pieces of metal plate have been bolted together atop a chainmail hauberk in a fashion that allows them to articulate freely, offering the wearer a good range of motion and a great degree of protection.
First Aid Kit
This small kit consists of a handful of chiurgical items, including bandages, compresses, and antiseptic paste. Properly used, it can aid in the natural healing process.
Dance of Sharp Angles

The multi-stage forging of this ring is a metallurgical mystery of yore. The structural integrity of this piecemeal ring seems to be severely compromised, with its layers of imprecisely interlocking plates of different metals, a few of which have accumulated a patina over the eons. Yet the band somehow retains its circular shape, while the notched rim layers may be twisted so that three layers impossibly swivel into merely two. There are no signs of friction or sound when you make any adjustment to these jagged layers, regardless of direction and degree. However, if the rings interlock multi-laterally, it pulls the wearer out of phase with reality, simultaneously pulling an ally from a different dimension to help absorb of an enemy's attacks.

This wooden stake has a crudely fashioned point and roots dangling from its head. When the proper command is given and the stake is thrown, it explodes on impact into a thick mass of tangled roots that entangle anyone slow or unlucky enough to be caught within. Its easy concealment, unassuming looks, and ability to stop a pursuer dead in their tracks has made this item popular among rogues and ne'er-do-wells.

This heavy, twisted bronze ring appears to have been part of some great machine. It is activated by heat, and rubbing the ring transposes the user with a target of choice. The ring burns out after one use, suggesting that it wasn't originally designed to transport living matter.
Odd Gloves
These six-fingered gloves are completely and utterly achromatic. Their singular lack of color is nearly hypnotic.
Stillness Cage

When a living animal is placed inside this birdcage, the device automatically activates, putting the creature into stasis. Theoretically it could preserve a living being indefinitely, though the cage's size limits this to very small creatures. This cage is inactive, and you do not have the means to reactivate it.
Viewshard

The shard of glass displays an image of three strangely-garbed children in a field. A sequence of them playing a simple ballgame repeats itself. After repeated viewings, you notice a small child standing further away in the field. This fourth child is looking directly at you. Her large eyes brim with fear.
Light Metal
This metal sphere is lighter than air. It is comfortably warm to the touch. If unsecured, it starts to float away, accelerating slowly. The origin of the sphere is unknown.

This tiny stone ball appears completely ordinary. No amount of close inspection reveals anything that stands out, nor any signs that this is anything more than it appears. Yet at any sign of mirth near the Antagonist, the stone ball will start howling at an ever-increasing intensity until it completely drowns out the laughter.
Ivroniar
A favorite among practical jokers, this unbreakable glass goblet always looks empty, even when it's full.
True Colors
When applied to a person's face, the plain black paint in this jar changes color to match their mood. The paint dries and flakes off the skin within fifteen minutes.
Knave's Card

A playing card shows a grinning Nibovian Child. When you rub your thumb over the card, it triggers an adaptive illusion that changes the face of the card, though you can't discover the trick to getting specific card faces to appear.
Nychthemeron Doll

It seems odd that someone would make a doll that resembles a nychthemeron. If you hug the plush, tentacled creature, it growls at you in the daytime but purrs softly at night. At other times it jitters oddly.
Globe of Zhrul
This synth globe clearly depicts an unknown world. The more you look at it, the more details you discover... as if the globe somehow enhances and concentrates your vision as you examine it.

An avian-looking fetus, still and apparently long dead, lies inside this thin membrane. The fetus seems to have been in an early stage of development. It can be consumed to gain knowledge long forgotten.

This strange, crudely crafted metal plate is lighter than it looks. A hole in its center glows with a soft, yellow radiance. Two handles nearby allow the user to carry the device. When  treated violently (such as being struck or thrown) the cypher's light hardens, and gravity settles harder on everything in the vicinity.

When applied to the skin, this graft modifies and thickens the molecular structure of the user's flesh. As a side effect, the skin takes on a gray pallor. The modification is harmless but begins to destabilize after a period of time, and will dissolve the user's skin if not removed in time. When taken off, the graft crumbles into dust.

This is a single glove with proboscises on its fingers. These proboscises have a disturbingly fleshy texture and color.The glove is a biofeedback data repository, particularly attuned to weapons of all kinds. Once used, the fleshy material withers and dies.

Even holding this fleshy, human-faced worm gives rise to an involuntary bout of nausea and weakness. When woken, the  worm can be thrown at a living being. It will attach itself to their flesh, releasing toxins into their bloodstream, causing instantaneous and powerful hallucinations - real enough to feel like memories to the victim. The hallucinations spin a tale of weakness that are vivid enough to translate into actual vulnerability.
Cypher Replicator

[An orb created from a series of synth blocks in various shapes that connect to each other via male and female tabs. The user can dismantle the orb and use the individual blocks to replicate the shape of a cypher in their inventory. Even if the duplicate is not identical, the finished object gives a viewer the sense that it is. In fact, for most people, it would be hard to tell the two objects apart.]​

This finely-made pin contains a minuscule device, to be worn on the chest. When pressure is applied to the pin, it activates the device, which causes rapid, flickering lights to appear around the wearer, making it difficult to target the user.
This thin, bluish token feels like it is made of stone, yet it is safe to consume, offering mental and bodily respite to the user.

The muddy red liquid in this vial swirls around lazily, guarded by a heavy metal stopper. It is potentially hazardous. Once ingested, the liquid penetrates the bloodstream and absorbs a portion of the user's vital energy. It then feeds these energies into another person, amplifying them so that the benefit to the recipient is greater than the cost to the donor.

This appears to be a combination of two devices. The first is a bulky, segmented band that folds to fit wrists of different sizes, which also appears to have heat-absorbing capabilities that make it cold to the touch. Seated inside the wristband is the second device - a small but bright emitter that can produce a powerful shield of pure light. The emitter superheats quickly before burning out, but thanks to the wristband will last longer than it otherwise would - and not burn a hole through your hand.

This brace structure is cleverly put together from pistons, miniature energy drives, and gravitational modifiers. When worn around the torso, it can be activated to support a good amount of the weight of any armor worn, giving the user more freedom of movement, though the energy sources in its different parts will burn out in a short amount of time.

This polished device is made of a material that seems like it is both metallic and crystalline in nature. Metal prongs stick out at one end. This cypher is used by holding the prongs to bare skin, allowing it to load information from the datasphere that increases the user's situational awareness.

Inside a small well-made box, you find a finger resting lightly on velvet bedding. The humanoid finger has been partially hollowed out. Synth wiring courses through it, keeping the skin taut. Peculiar pictographs decorate the matte-black box. A humanoid, after having eaten the finger, performs feats of juggling, drawing, and playing a violin. An additional set of cautionary pictographs greatly discourages severing a finger and placing the Prestidigitator in its stead.
This thin netting can be wrapped around any cypher, keeping it in a form of isolated stasis until it is ready to be used and preventing it from interfering with other cyphers in various nasty ways.

This eyeball and its stalk are clearly not human. The eyeball itself has an odd, opaque green color, but odder still is the fact that it maintains a moist, lifelike feel. Swallowing the eyeball - with some difficulty - imparts some of the vitality of whatever creature this was harvested from.
This plain, rough-cut crystal can be held against the forehead and acts as a focusing point for willpower, increasing the intensity of strikes that use mental energies.

This small stone statue of a handsome man is cunningly carved. Something resembling music plays from it, filling the minds of the user and its allies with the hope and belief that victory is not only possible, but inevitable - no matter what odds are being faced.
Datasphere Whisperer

This biomechanical device looks like it was cobbled together from the flesh of an alien lifeform and pieces of complex computational machinery. When activated, it scans the mind of the person holding it, using its biomechanical components to translate information tapped from the datasphere and relaying it to an intent listener, providing both knowledge and mental succor. Unfortunately, the heat generated by the machinery will quickly scorch and burn, rendering the device inert.
Datasphere Blast

A skein of alien characters shifts in filigree across the dark, glassy surface of this fist-sized globe. Gazing into it, you feel a cool radiance dancing at the edges of your thoughts. You look away and blink involuntarily as you realize the reflections of other beings appear... and it leaves you strangely cold. When triggered, this device transmits a burst of insight into the weaknesses of those around you before darkening forever.

This seemingly innocuous device would normally serve as a sleep aid, but some devious mind had the idea to overcharge it to maximum capacity using an energy tunneling device. When activated, it is capable of absorbing energy from anyone too close to it, though the excess of energy means that it burns out quickly, especially if used inexpertly.

This fine, blue-green powder is sprinkled into the eyes. The powder is actually composed of millions of nanites, which can then be activated by force of will, giving the user a sense of euphoria as well as an instant physical energy boost.
Ordinarily, this mossy green fungus grows in shallow, salty water. It chirps a soft song as it slowly dies outside of its natural habitat.
Beads of Mother Temaz

This long string of beads belonged to a midwife in Cliff's Edge. Each bead on the string is distinct and unique, representing one of the babies she delivered over the course of her long career. Touching one of the beads will put you into very brief mental contact with whoever that bead represents.
Fractal Lattice

This fine metal latticework appears to be a metal sieve of some kind. There is a faint breeze on one side of the lattice. You can't see any mechanical elements, but it seems to be drawing air through it and out the other side. There is a faint glow where the air is blowing outward. The glow increases whenever a breeze passes by.
Metallic Eye

This metallic, flower-like device consists of a short metal stalk with a mechanical eye at the end. It was given to you by Salimeri and can apparently be used as a key to enter the Anechoic Lazaret, a large golden structure in the Reef of Fallen Worlds.
Shadowstep

This set of brown spikes look like the roots of a plant. A pleasant flowery smell, accompanied by a gentle warmth, surrounds them. When placed against the user's feet they take root, driving themselves into the flesh. Once planted they allow one to move more swiftly, as if the spikes give their user a boost with each step.
A brown ring, seamlessly woven with overlapping scales. The ring is warm to the touch, and gently contracts when worn. It leaves the wearer with a feeling of promise to a greater unity.

This crystalline pyramid has several carvings of half-lidded eyes inscribed around the base. Hundreds of micro-hooks line the bottom, ensuring that it will firmly attach itself to whatever it's pressed against. When it is attached to the skin, it spawns extra-corporeal eyes that bob and weave nearby, gathering information for your consumption. You cannot understand everything they say - the information was not meant for a purely human mind.
Clawed Gauntlets
When held against the lower arms, these complex mechanical rods dig into the user's flesh. With a flick of the wrist, they produce long metal claws that enhance unarmed strikes.
Whispers

This carved gray crystal serves as a rough-hewn dagger. The crystal edge looks blunt and harmless... but it sharpens as you grasps it, and sharpens more the longer you focus on the blade. As you do so, you hear a soft whispering sound, coming from right behind your head... but when you turn around, you see no one behind you.
Gravitational Overseer

Abhumans of the Sagus Protectorate

Abhumans of the Sagus Protectorate - A Study of Savagery

"The creatures known as abhumans are believed to descend from human ancestors, but at some point in their history, they became something else - perhaps through mutation, directed breeding, or accelerated evolution. Unlike mutants, abhumans have rejected their humanity and live as beasts, though some are very clever. Nearly all of them are violent and cruel, preying upon humanity when they can.

Historically, two species of abhumans have been common in the Sagus Protectorate. The first is the vile murden, hunched and birdlike, with a sharp, dirty beak and a thick down of black feathers. Murdens subsist as thieves and murderers on the fringes of human society, rarely posing an organized threat to a community, but often ambushing lone victims or terrorizing isolated homesteads. They are incapable of speech, but they communicate with one another through a primitive form of telepathy that bleeds into the minds of everyone nearby, which can prove a dangerous distraction. Most of the time, murdens are notorious cowards, preferring to flee if the odds are not clearly in their favor.

The other abhuman species that once prospered here is the yovok. Short and squat, with jaundiced skin, yovoki hunt and kill for pleasure, and they eat whatever they kill. In the days when slavery was openly practiced in Sagus Cliffs, bands of yovoki were permitted to range across the frontier, raiding autochthonous tribes of humans and mutants and taking captives to be sold in the flesh markets of the Bloom. The vicious yovoki would sometimes rape their captives as well, and stories say that children were sometimes born from these pairings, tainting the bloodlines of certain families. After the rebellion of Chila the Great, slavery was outlawed in Sagus Cliffs, and the yovoki fled the Protectorate. They haven't been seen in centuries, but the people of Sagus still remember them, and any proof of a blood connection to these creatures is enough to destroy a family's reputation."

"Day 15:

Light.

Greasy, throbbing sunlight. In my eye. Tried to move. Couldn't.

Well, that was it, I reasoned. I wasn't just hung over. I was paralyzed.

Bound to happen eventually. Someone must have mistaken me for the lovely contortionist with the unagran tattoo, and twisted me like a length of rope to get at my tender parts.

Which, of course, I *did* appreciate. Even now.

I cleared my throat to call politely for help, and a husky voice mumbled something obscene (and somewhat half-hearted - it was dawn, after all) in my right ear. A bare hip settled comfortably into the palm of my left hand as another of my nameless companions got comfortable.

And then, of course, I realized the truth - I was not paralyzed. My limbs were merely pinned by the thirty or so strangers sharing the small bed with me.

What a relief."
