In the recording, the helmet's owner spoke of returning to a place called the Anchorage. I should try to find this place and speak to her people. They might be able to tell me more about her and the Cortex she mentioned.

Captain Janur told me that the owner of the helmet was named Achilli, but she wasn't particularly interested in Achilli's discovery. She did agree to let me keep the helmet. If I want to know what Achilli discovered, I'll have to access the Navigational Cortex myself.
The Cortex revealed Achilli's discovery - the Ninth World is actually the lascars' home. I should report this to Captain Janur right away.

Though Captain Janur didn't believe me at first, she finally realized that Home - the world that her people have been seeking for millennia - is just on the other side of the Maw portal. The lascars have abandoned the Anchorage to seek a new life in the Ninth World.
I tried to report my findings to the lascars, but when they discovered that I stole the Cortex, they angrily kicked me off the Anchorage. Because of my actions, Achilli's discovery is lost to them.

A fight broke out with the lascars as I was trying to verify Achilli's research. Now they've sealed the door to the Anchorage to prevent me from getting inside again. As a result, Achilli's discovery is lost to them.
I awakened in the Labyrinth when the Resonance Chamber was activated. Now I'll probably never be able to complete Achilli's work.

Based on the recording I found in the helmet, its owner was a lascar who came from the Anchorage, which I found on the far side of the Maw in Little Nihliesh. Captain Janur, the leader of the lascars, may be able to tell me more about the person who owned the helmet.

I gave the helmet to Captain Janur, as she requested. She erased all the recorded memories from the helmet, in accordance with some custom, so no one will ever know what its owner discovered. The helmet will be returned to the dead woman's family.
I tried to report my findings to the lascars but found the door to the Anchorage sealed on my return. They know I stole the Cortex, and they'll never let me back in now.
Unfortunately, it's forbidden for outsiders to access the Navigational Cortex.

In order to retrieve the data from the helmet, the Cortex needs to scan the helmet directly. I'll need to go through some sort of removal process to expose the Cortex in its housing in order to perform the scan.

Each stage of the removal process requires verification from the recessed pit on the Observation Deck (the first room I saw when I entered the Anchorage). That means I'll have to send someone over to the controls in the pit so they can send the verification signals... without anyone noticing.

I've learned that when the Cortex is being removed for maintenance, someone in the pit area of the Anchorage needs to press buttons in response to a panel lighting up. If this isn't done, the Cortex can't be removed.

I've discovered a secret Maw in the Shrine of Chila that leads into the depths of the Bloom... but it won't open until I feed it.

On returning to the Memovira, I spoke to the First and agreed that her plan was the better one. She began the process of activating the chamber.
On returning to the Memovira, I spoke to the First and decided that her plan - which would end up killing all of the castoffs - had to be stopped. She didn't take my decision very well.

The Decanted needs to recruit three people to fulfill its quota. I should make sure these recruits have attractive bodies - the Decanted doesn't seem concerned with any other traits.

When I find potential recruits, I should inform the Decanted, who is standing near the slave auction in the Memovira's Courtyard.

The Decanted has sent agents to retrieve the woman who was being used as a mouthpiece by the murdens. I should return tomorrow to see if they found her suitable.

Attunement completed
The Specter tells me I need attune to a force called the Tides. The tanks in this place allow me to mentally link to the creatures inside, each representing one of the five Tides.

By interacting with the tanks containing them, I can venture into the mind of each creature. Once connected, the Specter says I'll need to help the creature resolve a simulated situation - but that I should choose the path *I* prefer, not what I think think the creature prefers.

After completing my interaction with one creature, Sorrow fragments have infested the remaining control panels that allow me to form that mental link. The Specter or I will need to force them out before I can link with a creature.
With the Sorrow fragment driven out, I can now continue attunement by linking with the nearby creature.
Sorrow fragments continue to hinder my attempts to link to the remaining creatures. The Specter or I will need to drive another out of a control panel.
Once again, a creature has been cleared of the Sorrow's influence. I can now form a mental link with it.
With all of the Sorrow fragments now chasing the Specter and me, there's nothing to stop me from forming a mental link with the remaining creatures.
Somehow my actions have activated a glowing crystal placed at the back of the platform. The Specter says I just need to get to it to complete the attunement process.
As I laid my hand on the glimmering crystal, I was pulled into it in a flash of white light.
